title: Explicit Eigenvalue Regularization Improves Sharpness-Aware Minimization
publication_status_observed: 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024) per page 1 header; arXiv:2501.12666v1 [cs.LG] 22 Jan 2025
main_claims: SAM's implicit bias on sharpness reduction depends on the alignment between the perturbation vector and the top Hessian eigenvector, which is often insufficient in practice, limiting SAM's effectiveness.

A third-order SDE approximation of SAM dynamics reveals that the implicit regularisation includes second- and third-order terms, with the third-order term being the gradient of the top Hessian eigenvalue only when perturbation-eigenvector alignment is high.
Eigen-SAM, which explicitly aligns the perturbation with the leading eigenvector, achieves more effective sharpness reduction and improved generalisation compared to SAM.
methodology: The authors extend the second-order SDE framework of Compagnoni et al. (2023) to a third-order SDE for SAM by including third-order Taylor expansion terms (Theorem 4.1). They prove a PAC-Bayes bound linking top Hessian eigenvalue to generalisation error (Theorem 3.1). They introduce Align(epsilon, v1) as a measure of perturbation-eigenvector alignment and prove that when alignment is 1-O(rho), SAM's drift includes the gradient of the top eigenvalue. Eigen-SAM is proposed to improve alignment and validated on CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet, and other benchmarks.
key_results: The third-order SDE (Theorem 4.1) achieves lower approximation error than the prior second-order SDE for the same rho, and ρ = O(η^{1/3}) is required compared to ρ = O(η^{1/2}).
Corollary 4.1.1 proves that when perturbation-eigenvector alignment ≥ 1-O(ρ), SAM's trajectory implicitly regularises the gradient norm (scale ρ) and top eigenvalue (scale ρ²/2) simultaneously.
Empirical experiments show that Eigen-SAM reduces top eigenvalue more reliably than SAM and achieves superior test accuracy, though specific numbers are not in the portion read.
limitations: The third-order SDE analysis requires regularity assumptions (e.g., bounded third-order derivatives, positive eigenvalue gap) that may not hold in all practical settings.
Computing the top eigenvector of the Hessian is expensive; Eigen-SAM uses power iteration intermittently to manage cost.
The alignment analysis is theoretical and the regime ρ = O(η^{1/3}) may not match practical hyperparameter choices.
relevance_to_rq: This paper provides a mechanistic analysis of why SAM's sharpness reduction may be incomplete in practice (poor perturbation-eigenvector alignment), which directly speaks to the RQ's question of whether SAM's OOD gains are mainly due to sharpness reduction. If SAM does not reliably reduce sharpness, the residual OOD benefit may stem from other mechanisms such as representation stability.
